title: Guardrails before code
summary: Set up CLAUDE.md, a quality-gates contract, hooks (secret and destructive-command guard, format and lint on edit, typecheck and tests on stop, spend and context budget guard, live cost status line, token ledger), human commit checks (husky, lint-staged, commitlint), Dependabot, CodeQL, daily API contract check, post-deploy smoke tests, a design-time threat model, a runbook and a production-readiness record, 28 tests for the guardrail hooks themselves, subagents (test-writer, code-reviewer, security-reviewer, api-scout), slash commands, ADRs and CI before writing any app code.
humanInterventions: Adam chose the problem, the stack (Next.js on Vercel) and the guardrail set.

title: Quality tooling and gates
summary: Wired the quality gates from docs/quality-gates.md so they fail for real: strict type-checked ESLint (complexity, a11y, no process.env outside src/env.ts), a zod-validated env, static security headers and CSP (ADR 0003), Vitest coverage thresholds, Stryker mutation scoped to src/lib/colour, Playwright with axe and header smoke tests, a first-load JS budget with size-limit (ADR 0004), commitlint and husky, a guard hook that asks before the agent edits its own guardrails, and a weighted-token budget guard. Every gate was broken on purpose to prove it fails. Honest notes: (1) the size budget was first set to 150 kB without measuring a baseline; the real Next 16 and React 19 floor was 180.35 kB, so the gate itself exposed it and it became 200 kB with ADR 0004. (2) The CORS assumption for canvas image access was caught at plan review, before any image code, and is still an open spike recorded in ADR 0002 and the CSP. (3) The budget guard was miscalibrated: it counted cache reads at full weight and blocked a session at 10.3M mostly-cached tokens; it now counts weighted tokens (cache reads at 0.1) with tests, and the block message tells the agent to ask Adam. (4) CI could not install at all: size-limit ^12 against @size-limit/file 13 failed npm ci with a peer conflict, so every job was red until the code review caught it. Two independent reviews ran twice; the second pass found that my guard rewrite had regressed 15 shell write forms the earlier guard blocked, which is fixed with tests. The regex guard is documented as a tripwire with its known gaps listed, and several Should items from the second review (injectable trust check for the bypass-secret test, project-specific Vercel host pattern, SHA-pinning all actions in the smoke job, PowerShell matcher, verifying hook ask in bypass mode) are deliberately left open and listed in the PR.
humanInterventions: Adam raised the size budget to 200 kB after the baseline was measured.
Adam's plan review caught the CORS assumption before any image code was written.
Adam spotted the budget guard blocking on cache reads and asked for weighted tokens.
Adam reduced the guard-bypass scope to a 20-minute time box and chose the tripwire framing, and chose docs-only handling for the smoke secret and pinning only the two token-holding actions.

title: Browse and search Morris & Co. designs from the V&A
summary: Home page with debounced search and a responsive grid, a design page with a large IIIF image and metadata (designers kept separate from manufacturers), allowlisted /api/vam/search, /api/vam/object/[id] and /api/health route handlers, a pure V&A client (5 s timeout including the body, one retry, no redirects, JSON-only and size-capped), zod schemas mapped to our own domain types, a structured logger, root and design error and not-found pages, ADR 0002 accepted (images load directly from framemark with crossOrigin always set, final CSP), the first live contract test and an @external canvas test proving getImageData works on a real framemark image. First-load JS 180.95 kB of 200 kB, 453 unit tests, 23 e2e tests with axe on every page. Honest notes: (1) the V&A filter changed during planning: the person filter was the first idea, api-scout showed Morris & Co. as an organisation (A1365) is the better set, and that the API has no OR (both filters is an AND), so the organisation alone is used. Adam's premise that Dearle appears only in the organisation set was wrong: he is in both. (2) The independent code review found a real bug that all 404 tests missed: an error thrown inside a use-cache function loses its class crossing the cache boundary, so every V&A failure including not-found became a 500. Every layer that could have caught it was mocked. The fix returns an Outcome value across the boundary, and new unmocked @external @smoke tests hit the real routes. (3) Next 16 use cache is in-memory and best-effort on serverless, so stale-while-revalidate alone is not a dependable cache or stale-serve strategy on Vercel; CDN Cache-Control headers were added and the limit is documented in the runbook. (4) Zod is not shipped to the browser (it would blow the ~20 kB bundle headroom), so client components use small hand-written type guards in src/lib with tests. (5) Not done: no per-client rate limit (a Vercel Firewall rule is the documented follow-up), and the search hook's state machine is only covered by e2e, not as a pure reducer.
humanInterventions: Adam approved the acceptance criteria with three changes: drop the in-memory last-good map (per-instance and ephemeral on Vercel), widen the filter from William Morris the person to Morris & Co. and show the designer on every card and page, and cache the /api/health V&A check for 60 s so it cannot become an amplification route.
Adam chose the scoped ESLint override for the one plain wrapper after the brief (plain , not next/image) collided with the no-img-element rule and the ban on eslint-disable.
The guard hook blocked me when I tried to edit docs/quality-gates.md and the workflow files through a shell script; I redid them with the Edit tool so Adam was asked.

Agent mistakes that were self-caught, not human-caught: I wrote an eslint-disable comment twice (CLAUDE.md forbids it) and removed both; I let the plan pre-assume a last-good cache that the docs show does not persist on serverless; and my own new race-condition e2e test found a stuck "Loading…" button in the search hook.
The review fixes were not prompted by Adam: the independent reviewers found the cache-boundary 500 bug and the others.

Adam caught that I had dropped the Claude-Model trailer from later commits after reading a session instruction about attribution lines as covering it. He clarified in CLAUDE.md that it is a required project metadata trailer, and had me add it back to the four unpushed commits that lacked it.

Adam asked for the no-inline-disable rule to be enforced mechanically (linterOptions.noInlineConfig) after I wrote two eslint-disable comments despite the CLAUDE.md ban, and asked for the six friction entries for this feature.

CI caught a lint failure I never saw locally: type-aware lint depended on route types in .next/types left by earlier builds, the same class of bug as the 001 LayoutProps failure. Fixed at the root (typegen in lint, plus npm run verify:clean).

The Claude PR review caught that my Outcome fix for lost error classes made failures cacheable, so a failed revalidation could overwrite a good entry and defeat serve-stale. Failures now throw inside the cache with the code in error.digest; only successes and 404s are cached.
